name: crew-three
title: A Cattain starts three crew threads, rests on them, and keeps its digest
about: The person asks miso, in its own thread, to fix three flaky tests, one thread each. The fake CLI calls start_crew_thread three times through Neko's own MCP server. The three crew threads nest under miso in the sidebar and list in its Overview; miso's thread rests on them ("Waiting on its crew"). As each crew thread's turn ends miso is woken, in at most two batches, one note "Woken by …" for each; the fake Cattain rewrites DIGEST.md, which the Digest tab shows. The store says miso started all three.

steps.text: Fix the three flaky tests, one thread each [fake:mcp] mcp neko start_crew_thread {"title":"Fix test one","brief":"Fix the first flaky test [fake:work:6]"} ; mcp neko start_crew_thread {"title":"Fix test two","brief":"Fix the second [fake:work:7]"} ; mcp neko start_crew_thread {"title":"Fix test three","brief":"Fix the third [fake:work:8]"}

steps.expect: Three crew threads nest under miso and list in its Overview; miso rests on them

steps.name: crew-at-work
steps.expect: miso with its crew at work: nested in the sidebar, Crew 3 in the Overview, the waiting line

sh.run: /usr/bin/sqlite3 "$data/neko.sqlite3" "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE started_by = 'cat_miso' AND cat_id = 'cat_miso' AND parent_id IS NULL"
test "$(grep -c 'is started in your crew' fake-record.jsonl)" -ge 3 && echo yes || echo no

steps.expect: The store has three crew threads miso started; each start answered with the cue to end the turn
miso is woken by all three and rewrites its digest

sh.run: n=$(grep '"stdin"' fake-record.jsonl | grep -c 'neko-wake kind=."crew' || true); test "$n" -ge 1 -a "$n" -le 2 && echo yes || echo "no: $n wakes"

steps.expect: miso was woken in at most two batches
The Digest tab shows what miso wrote, with its age

steps.name: digest
steps.expect: The digest after the update: New lists the three crew threads, done
